title: dev/check_function_signatures: tests are skipped on Windows because the check runs only in the Ubuntu lint job
answers: Why is the function signature check test skipped on Windows?
Do I need to add Windows path handling to dev/check_function_signatures.py?
Where is the function-signature compatibility check run in CI?
body:
Path: The function-signature compatibility check in dev/ compares changed Python function signatures against a git revision (e.g. HEAD^1), via dev/check_function_signatures.py:get_changed_python_files and get_file_content_at_revision. It is a developer lint tool, not runtime MLflow code.
Rule: Tests for this dev tool are excluded on Windows with a module-level pytestmark skipif(sys.platform == "win32") in tests/dev/test_check_function_signatures.py. Do not add Windows-specific path normalization (e.g. backslash to forward slash for git object specs) to dev/check_function_signatures.py, because the script only runs in the Ubuntu lint job.
Constraints: Applies to dev/ tooling that only runs in Linux CI. Does not apply to mlflow/ package code, which must still work on Windows. If the check is ever run on Windows, remove the skip and add path-separator handling with a PureWindowsPath regression test.
applies: Developer lint/tooling under dev/ and its tests in tests/dev/; not for runtime library code.
says: Function signature check test suite is skipped when running tests on Windows machines.
Developer test suite on Windows skips the function signature compatibility verification tests.
Do not require Windows path compatibility for developer lint tools restricted to Linux.

Windows-specific path normalization is excluded from dev/check_function_signatures.py because the script executes only in the Ubuntu lint CI job. Applies only to developer tooling under dev/ and tests/dev/, without relaxing Windows support requirements for runtime mlflow package code.
